findings.body:
`InsecureSkipVerify: true` is set on the shared `http.Client` returned by `NewClient()` with no environment, config, or build-tag guard. Every consumer — including production if this binary is deployed there — will accept any TLS certificate on the ledger connection, enabling MITM against ledger traffic (credentials, balances, postings).

The comment claims this is staging-only (TICKET-77), but nothing in the code enforces that. Either gate the skip behind an explicit non-default staging flag, or trust the staging CA via `RootCAs` / cert pinning so verification stays on.

```suggestion
			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12}, // load staging CA into RootCAs if needed
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this unconditionally disables TLS certificate verification for every caller of `NewClient()`, in every environment.

## Why this is blocking

`tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}` is wired into the shared HTTP client with no environment, build-tag, or config gate. The comment says "staging" and cites TICKET-77, but the code path is global: any production (or otherwise non-staging) use of `ledger.NewClient()` will accept any certificate, including a MITM on the ledger connection.

That is a concrete confidentiality/integrity failure for whatever the ledger client sends or receives (auth material, balances, postings), not a style nit.

## What would make this acceptable

Gate the skip on an explicit staging-only signal (env var / config flag that defaults to verify-on), or pin the staging CA / use a custom `RootCAs` pool instead of skipping verification entirely. Keep production on verified TLS.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
